chapter: Ben Pollack band and New York
title: Jack Teagarden at Uptons' speakeasy
summary: Pee Wee Russell brings him and Bud Freeman to hear Teagarden play 'Diane', and he tells the Pollack band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But the thing that happened with the Ben Pollack band was we were playing at the Park Central Hotel at the time and we hadn't gone into the Park Central yet. We just finished at another place. We were on one night stands, that's right. Atlantic City and all around and so forth. And came back to New York and Peewee Russel called Bud Freeman and me up one afternoon. And he said, hey you guys, come on down here to Uptons' Speak Easy. It was a speak easy down on 50th Street, 51st I mean and Broadway and 7th. He says there's a trombone player here the greatest thing you've ever heard in your life if you come down.

Now we said, now watch it Pete, be careful. So he said, come on down here and find out. And so we got down there and he says I want you to meet Jack Teagarden. He's from down Texas way, Oklahoma and Texas, and Jack had a cap in his hand and was sitting there drinking and he had his trombone and a cloth case. And Jack was quiet and pleasant and nice and he was talking about music. And he said to me, you know, he
said, you know, play, you know. Play something for us Jack you know.
So sure enough he got the horn out Jack Teagarden did in this speak easy and he started to play a tune called 'Diane'.
But the way he phrased it was really something, that tone you know. (SINGS TUNE)..

And man we listen to this guy blow that horn and we flipped. He was too much. What a great stylist he was. A great personality. A beautiful guy. So we heard him do this and we went back on the job that night. I guess we were still at this 'Little Club' it was called on 43rd Street. And we told the guys about it you know. And we had already made arrangements to have a jam session after we finished our job.
So we told the rest of the guys in Pollack's band about this great trombone player. So all the guys came you know to the jam session that we had at some silly hotel. I can't remember the name of it.
And sure enough we had a jam session and Teagarden got out that trombone and everybody, knocked everybody cold, with his beautiful blowing.
